sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Litavis (Litavus) is a Continental Celtic goddess. Not much is known of her. Her name seems tied to words for earth or broad, which would make her a deity of the wide world. The source sometimes names her the partner of the god Cicollus. The Romans saw Cicollus as close to their own god Mars. The invading legions did not rename Litavis as they reworked so many continental divinities.
